cross_box.conclusion: SUPERSEDED 2026-08-10 (afternoon). The band-overlap reading recorded here was the WRONG INSTRUMENT and the retraction built on it has been withdrawn. The #95 band answers 'how much could this metric move if BATCH COMPOSITION changed'; these parity runs hold batch composition fixed (same rows, same order, same batch size 16), so batch noise is not the source of variation between boxes and a band built from it cannot license 'indistinguishable'. A third run settled it: b650 rebuilt on production's exact frozen stack and run on CUDA flips the SAME THREE ARTICLES at 4.5, same direction, same specificity 0.9662 -- and a proximity control rules out 'whatever is nearest the cut' (of 18 production rows in [4.30, 4.50) only those 3 flip, while one at 4.4870, CLOSER to the threshold, does not). The between-box difference is SYSTEMATIC and article-specific, and the 2026-08-09 conclusion 'b650 is cleared at 4.0 and NOT at 4.5' stands as written. It does not touch #102: the box effect is 0.0068 specificity against a 4.0->4.5 gain of 0.054, so it governs which machine may produce a number, never what the number implies. See docs/evidence/2026-08-10-b650-gpu-production-stack-parity.md.

constraint_found.what: MAX_NORMALIZATION_RAW_MIN = 4.5 bounds the op-point from above.
constraint_found.detail: tests/unit/test_normalization_invariant.py requires normalization.json stats.raw_min == the filter's tier threshold, and NexusMind/src/scoring/production_scorer.py rejects a fit with raw_min > 4.5 (strict >, so exactly 4.5 is accepted) -- falling back to score_scale_factor with only a log warning. uplifting v7's committed fit has raw_min 4.0, n=18130. So 4.5 is reachable but sits ON the bound with ZERO margin; 4.75 and 5.0 are NOT reachable without raising the constant in BOTH repos.
constraint_found.consequence: any op-point move requires refitting normalization.json at the new anchor in the same change.
